crystallography.goal: Two neighbouring planes of atoms, a distance a apart, scatter X-rays of wavelength λ arriving at a glancing angle θ. The rays reinforce when the extra path between the planes is a whole number n of wavelengths. Write a.
crystallography.name: Bragg reflection condition
crystallography.ask: Find d in ångströms for copper Kα (L = 1.5406 Å), first order (n = 1), reflecting at t = 0.3067 rad.
crystallography.method: The ray scattered by the deeper plane travels 2d·sin θ further; the waves add up when that is a whole number of wavelengths.

crystal_growth_physics.goal: A crystal grows at its front only as fast as its latent heat L (per kilogram) can be carried away up the crystal, of density ρ, which conducts heat k watts per metre per kelvin down a gradient G. Write the growth speed v.
crystal_growth_physics.name: Stefan condition at the front
crystal_growth_physics.ask: Find v in mm/h for silicon: k = 22 W/(m·K), G = 1500 K/m, R = 2330 kg/m³, L = 1.8e6 J/kg.
crystal_growth_physics.method: At the front the heat conducted away, k·G per square metre, must equal the latent heat set free, ρ·L·v.

geometric_optics.goal: A thin lens of refractive index n has two surfaces of radii R _ 1 and R _ 2 (positive when the centre of the curve lies beyond the surface). Write its power P, one over its focal length.
geometric_optics.name: Lensmaker's equation
geometric_optics.ask: Find P in dioptres for a fused silica lens, n = 1.458, with A = 0.5 m and B = −0.5 m.
geometric_optics.method: Each surface bends the light by (n − 1)/R; for a thin lens the two bends simply add.
